name: Sovereign Archdragon

notes.saves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

items.name: Sanctified Sight
items.text: The dragon can automatically detect if a creature, effect, or item is sanctified, and whether it's holy or unholy.

items.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic
Mentalist Counterspell
items.text:
Trigger The dragon is targeted by a mental effect they're aware of

---
Effect The dragon immediately attempts to counteract the triggering effect (counteract modifier +38, counteract rank 10).

items.name: Violent Retort
items.text:
Trigger A creature within the sovereign dragon's reach critically hits the dragon

---
Effect The sovereign dragon makes a claw or tail Strike against the creature, after applying all the effects of the critical hit to the dragon.

items.name: Change Shape
items.text:
The dragon takes on the appearance of any Small or Medium humanoid. This doesn't change its Speed or attack and damage bonuses with its Strikes, but might change the damage type its Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning).

---

items.name: Coiling Frenzy
items.text: The dragon makes one claw Strike and one tail Strike in either order, each against the same target. If either Strike hits, the dragon can attempt to Grab the target with that limb as a free action. The dragon can have up to three creatures Grabbed or Restrained at a time; one in each of their front claws, and a third with their tail.

items.name: Draconic Momentum
items.text: The dragon recharges Sovereign's Rebuke whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.

items.name: Gleaming Armor
items.text:
Frequency once per hour

---
Effect The dragon's armor glows with a golden light. The dragon gains a +2 status bonus to AC and resistance 25 to acid, cold, electricity, fire, and sonic damage. Each enemy in a 20-foot emanation must succeed at a DC 46 Fortitude save save or be Dazzled. All these effects last until the end of the dragon's next turn.

items.name: Inspire Envoy
items.text:
Frequency once per day

---
Effect The dragon chooses a mortal and offers their august blessing in exchange for the creature carrying out a specific directive, such as defeating a tyrant or protecting a sacred site. If the creature agrees, until its next daily preparations, it gains a +3 status bonus to the dragon's choice of attack rolls, AC, or all of the following: Perception, Will saves, and Charisma-based skill checks. The dragon can Dismiss this benefit, which they're swift to do if the mortal dares to defy the dragon's directive.

Effect: Inspire Envoy

items.name: Sovereign's Rebuke
items.text: The dragon unleashes a roar charged with psychic energy, dealing 24d6 mental damage in a 60-foot cone (DC 46 basic Will save save). A creature who fails their save is also Confused for 1 round (or Controlled by the dragon for 1 round on critical failure). The dragon can't use Sovereign's Rebuke again for 1d4 rounds.

text:
There were supposedly dragons of pure elemental earth, once. These were imperial dragons who, like their other elemental counterparts, came to the Universe, lived, and died, their bodies becoming part of the continent. As fire became lava, wood became forests, water the seas, lakes, and rivers, and metal the veins of precious minerals, so earth became the land, the stone, the mountains. By way of logic, if there exist such environments and entities today, then earth dragons must exist too. Or have existed, once upon a primeval time.

And yet among the imperial dragons today there are only sovereign dragons, who leave serpentine skeletons behind upon death in place of rock, stone, or land. The dragons' innate spellcasting, weakness to unheated iron, and other traits highly suggest that they're associated with elemental earth. The rest of their powers have little to no such association, instead centered on the mysteries of the metaphysical spirit and mind.

There's no clear explanation for why sovereign dragons are the way they are today. Some guess it might have been a deal to fulfill personal ambition, to go from those tasked with selecting rulers to becoming the rulers themselves. Others wonder if the lands of Tian Xia were corrupted in the past, and the earth dragons walked away from their elemental natures to save themselves. Perhaps they too became empyreal dragons, but then returned to the lands of mortals when no suitable ruler rose to the throne.
